attempts.raw_response: After that time, gently slide a thin spatula under the fish. If the skin releases easily and is crisp and browned, it's ready to flip. If it sticks, give it another minute. Once flipped, cook the other side for just 2-3 minutes, as the flesh will continue cooking from residual heat. The result is a perfectly cooked, flaky interior with a beautifully charred, intact skin. Serve immediately with a squeeze of lemon or a simple herb butter.

pair.human_continuation: The fish is ready to be flipped when the skin no longer sticks to the grill. Generally, a fish that weighs 1/2 to 1 pound (.22 to .45 kg) will take about 5 to 7 minutes per side. Larger fish, 1 1/2 to 2 pounds (.7 to .9 kg), can take around twice that amount of time. Another general guideline for whole fish is 10 minutes of cooking per side, per inch of thickness. To turn the fish, have your tongs in your “off” hand and a big spatula (oiled on both sides) in your good hand. Gently turn the fish over. It should come off the grates cleanly. If not, don’t force it.
pair.prefix: If possible, set the tail farthest away from the flames, as the skinnier, tail-end of the fish cooks faster than the rest. The crucial step is what you do after you place the fish on the hot grill: You wait. Fight the impulse to mess with the fish and move it around -- you'll rip the skin, lose some flesh, and throw off the cooking. Instead, stand there for 3-4 minutes.
